newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais mistrust Banharn, want former PM Chuan-polls.
newsitem.headline: Thais mistrust Banharn, want former PM Chuan-polls.

text.p: Outgoing Thai prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa ranks lowest in terms of integrity and capability among top politicians, two opinion polls showed on Thursday.
A Thammasat University poll gave Banharn the lowest rating in integrity and capability of Thailand's 11 party leaders, the Bangkok Post reported.
Opposition Democrat Party leader and former premier Chuan Leekpai topped the list in both categories, according to the survey of 275 people in Bangkok.
The poll also showed Banharn's Chart Thai Party was the least trusted party.

An Assumption University poll, which surveyed 724 companies via the Internet, showed the majority of business people prefer Chuan's Democrat Party to form the next government if there were fresh elections.

When asked which leader they would choose from the current six coalition parties to be the next prime minister, 67 percent chose Nam Thai Party leader and foreign minister Amnuay Viravan, followed by Defence Minister and New Apiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh with nearly 15 percent.
Banharn announced on Saturday he would step down as prime minister in seven days after choosing an appropriate successor.

He agreed to resign in exchange for support from his coalition in a no-confidence vote after a bruising three-day attack on him in parliament. Banharn won the vote 207-180 after he announced his resignation.

The coalition parties are at loggerheads over Banharn's successor. Chavalit, whose party is the second-biggest in the coalition after Chart Thai, is seen as the front runner while most of the Chart Thai support party elder Pramarn Adireksarn. Amnuay is seen as a possible compromise candidate.

The Assumption poll showed nearly 38 percent of business people want a dissolution of parliament to break the current political deadlock. Another 26 percent want the coalition to step aside and allow the opposition to form a new government.
Only six percent backed the current coalition government.
Political analysts have said if the coalition partners cannot agree on a successor to Banharn, he may decide to dissolve the house and call fresh elections.
